summary: Adds rows after the last row that holds data.
description: Pass a sheet and the whole sheet is examined, with the write starting in column 1; pass a range and only its cells are, with the write landing on the range's columns — data elsewhere on the sheet no longer decides where the block goes.

Nothing is overwritten: the write starts one row below the last one holding data, and `0` and `false` count as data. The sheet gains rows when it is too short for the result. Unlike `Sheet#appendRow`, which takes one row at a time, the whole block is written in a single call.
A cell whose text starts with `=` is written as a formula, not as text — the same rule the editor follows.
A failure inside the write — the service unavailable, the sheet gone — comes back as the error the service raised, with its stack. The document lock is released either way.

params.target: The sheet to append to, or the range to append within.
params.values: A matrix of rows: one array per row, all of the same length.
params.options: `afterFrozenRows` starts the write below the frozen rows when the data ends before them.

returns: the sheet, so calls can be chained.

throws.InvalidSheetException: the first argument is neither a sheet nor a range.
throws.TypeError: the values are not a matrix with rows of equal length.
